title: The micrograph
does: What it does. Reads the 16-bit TIFF, stretches it to 8 bit on its 0.5/99.5 percentiles, and crops the databar off: 6144×4096 px survive.
cost: Cost. A percentile stretch, not min/max: a hot pixel or the crack itself at 0 would otherwise own the range and flatten the background texture Otsu needs downstream.
figs: p01_micrograph.png
8-bit, after the 0.5/99.5 percentile stretch and the field-of-view crop.

title: Why the next step exists: the illumination
does: What it does. Nothing yet — this is the quantity flatten_background is about to subtract.
cost: Why it matters. A single global threshold on the raw image would track this drift instead of the crack.
figs: p02_background.png
The Gaussian background estimate at sigma=40 over this crop, false-coloured. It spans 92.8 to 139.3 grey levels across 512 px — drift of that size sits on top of every crack.
p01_micrograph.png
The same crop, as captured, for comparison.

title: flatten_background
does: What it does. Subtracts the blurred copy, so what is left is local contrast.
cost: What it costs. It is a high-pass filter, so it also erases anything wider than its own radius. The detector's own docstring measures this: pixels that are genuinely pitch black (raw 0–4) come out near 122 of 255 after flattening, indistinguishable from mid-grey matrix. That single sentence is why steps 5 and 6 exist.
figs: p03_flat.png
The flattened image: raw minus the background above, rescaled to 8 bit on its own 0.5/99.5 percentiles.

title: The darkness cut, at one radius
does: What it does. Keeps a pixel if the denoised flat image is below min(Otsu, median − 5×MAD), OR if the raw 8-bit image is below 10. Taking the lower of Otsu and the robust bar is what stops Otsu flagging half the frame on a unimodal histogram.
cost: What it buys, on this crop. precision 0.9900, recall 0.2587, IoU 0.2580 against the hand paint. Almost everything it marks is crack; it finds about a quarter of it.

The absolute-darkness term alone carries 15 px here and 233,102 px frame-wide. At corpus scale it supplies roughly half of all the recall the detector has, and its threshold of 10 has no provenance; raising it is additive but three instruments disagree about whether to, so it stays put.
figs: p04_cut40.png
carries 1,808 px in this crop (0.69% of it) · 483,991 px in the whole frame

title: The same cut at each of the seven radii
does: What it does. Re-flattens the image at sigma = 5, 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 320 and takes the identical cut at each. A crack is only reliably dark at the scales near its own width, so one radius sees one band.
cost: “New” counts pixels no earlier rung and not the absolute-darkness term had already claimed, taken in ascending sigma, so the seven new-counts sum to the union and no pixel is counted twice. Each rung is produced by calling the installed detector with that one rung in its ladder; the OR of the seven plus the absolute term is asserted equal, bit for bit, to the mask the pipeline itself returned.

title: Their union — the change v1.49 made
does: What it does. ORs the seven cuts. It is a strict superset of the single-radius mask by construction, so it cannot drop a pixel the older build kept — checked, not assumed: 0 px lost across the 26 labelled tiles and across 6,669,145 hand-painted pixels on 12 full frames.
cost: What it buys, on this crop. +2,081 px here and +183,944 px frame-wide. precision 0.9900 → 0.8138, recall 0.2587 → 0.4574, IoU 0.2580 → 0.4141. Over the 26 labelled tiles the same change reads IoU 0.2979 → 0.3344 pooled, and it costs no new tuned constant: the ladder is every scale, not a chosen subset.
What it costs. Seven flattening passes instead of one: 12.7 s of this frame's 130.2 s. Above sigma=64 the background is estimated on a decimated copy, which is what keeps that from being 67 s.
figs: p06_union.png
carries 3,889 px in this crop (1.48% of it) · 667,935 px in the whole frame

title: clean_mask
does: What it does. Drops components of 13 px or fewer, opens with a disk of radius 1, closes with a disk of radius 3, fills holes.
cost: What it costs here. removes 168 px, adds back 42 (the closing and the hole fill are extensive), net -126 px in this crop.
figs: p07_clean.png
carries 3,763 px in this crop (1.44% of it) · 666,796 px in the whole frame

title: The 40 px region floor
does: What it does. extract_candidates labels the clean mask with connectivity=2 and keeps only components of at least 40 px, renumbering the survivors 1..N. 465 candidate regions survive on this frame.
cost: What it costs here. 249 px in this crop.

And what does not happen next. The region classifier is USE_REGION_CLASSIFIER = False, so every one of those regions is kept. Deleting it won on all four metrics with zero free parameters; six region-level precision rules tried since all scored well on 512 px crops and then deleted 54–75% of hand-painted crack on the 48 full frames.
figs: p08_floor.png
carries 3,514 px in this crop (1.34% of it) · 662,941 px in the whole frame

title: Pass 2
does: What it does. With a crack mask now in hand, proposes concavity, bridge-corridor and interior-fill candidates relative to it, scores them with the unified model, and folds the accepted ones in. 154 proposed on this frame, 129 accepted.
cost: What it buys. +41,369 px frame-wide (5.87% of the final mask) and 0 px in this crop. The second pair of panels is a different place, not a different stage, and is shown because a panel of the main crop alone would read as the stage doing nothing anywhere.

title: The emitted mask
does: What it does. Unions every kept region into one boolean mask and saves it. Area fraction 2.799% on this frame, 1.341% in this crop.
figs: p10_emitted.png
carries 3,514 px in this crop (1.34% of it) · 704,310 px in the whole frame

title: The measured output
does: What it does. Re-labels the emitted mask and measures every component: area, tip-to-tip geodesic, skeleton length, mean and max width, tortuosity, and whether it runs off the frame edge.
cost: What it costs. 452 rows on this frame, 16 in this crop. Length is a bracket, not a value: 2.65% of regions on this frame touch the edge, but they are 29.57% of the crack area and 20.43% of the length. No scale bar was recovered for this frame, so every column here is pixels, not microns.
figs: p11_regions.png
One colour per measured crack; grey is a component at or below the 25 px speck floor, which the measurement step drops. 16 components in this crop, 0 of them specks.

title: Against the hand paint, and where the recall goes
does: On this crop: precision 0.8557, recall 0.4346, IoU 0.4049. One crop is not a corpus figure.
cost: The two stages worth marking are the first row and everything else. On this crop the darkness cut owns 95.19% of all missed paint and the two morphology/area filters own 4.81% between them; over the 48 hand-painted full frames the same decomposition reads 96.02% and 3.98%. Tuning the morphology cannot reach the problem.

Reproduce every panel and every number on this page: make_flowchart.py beside this file, run under the detector environment. It asserts its own ladder against the pipeline's output and asserts the loss buckets are exhaustive before it writes anything.
note: How to read any number on this page. These are one crop of one frame, shown because the stages are comparable on it. The corpus figures, over the 26 hand-labelled tiles, move further with the aggregation than with any method change ever measured in this project, so a score is unreadable without its row and its tolerance:aggregationprecisionrecallF1IoUpooled over all pixels0.41820.62520.50120.3344median over the 26 tiles0.80560.76230.59220.4208median over 13 specimens0.78970.71590.54180.3715median over specimens, 2 px tolerance0.89880.80250.66330.4962A perfectly placed trace caps at IoU 0.4993 pooled and 0.5498 median over tiles on these labels, so 0.4208 is 84% of what the labels permit, not 42% of perfect. IoU and clDice are both width-gameable here — a no-information dilation to 1.5× area moves clDice +0.0478 on 13 of 13 specimens — so the metric to compare methods on is skeleton-F1 at a 2 px tolerance, where this detector scores 0.5507.
